findings.title: Represent unknown host quota snapshot explicitly
findings.issue: Prefix allows absence of a snapshot through nulls, but quotas mandate four exact reserved integers and generated numeric remaining. If the guest dies before a trusted ledger snapshot, the host cannot know sample/identity/marker reservations. Partial journal bytes do not recover a fully reserved failed row. Fixed policy reservations are known, but substituting initial values or full limits as the actual reserved vector invents a fact.
findings.requiredChange: Allow reserved=null as whole-vector unknown and generate remaining=null in that case. Keep fixed policy slots and pool limits independently known. An exact vector must refer to an actual trusted reservation snapshot; upper bounds require explicit bound typing and cannot silently replace exact values.
findings.tests: NOT_RUN: host unobserved/partial-write failure with no ledger snapshot produces null reserved/remaining; exact known-empty and known-filled snapshots retain numeric values; reject independently supplied remaining.

findings.title: Define consistency predicates for named retrieval failure reasons
findings.issue: Only none and generic incomplete are constrained. As written, [exited,0,null] with both completeness flags true can carry signaled or truncated_both while satisfying every stated validation predicate. Named reasons then contradict the same receipt process/capture fields, undermining the typed diagnostic record.
findings.requiredChange: Define minimum consistency rules: signaled requires signaled process; exit_nonzero requires exited nonzero code; truncated_stdout/stderr/both require their corresponding incomplete flag pattern. Define reasonable minimum conditions for spawn_error/read_error/unknown without requiring the serializer to establish external provenance. Preserve process outcome independence from capture completeness and use an explicit documented priority if several failures coexist.
findings.tests: NOT_RUN: reject exited0+signaled, exited0+exit_nonzero, complete capture+truncated reason and mismatched truncated-side flags; retain nonzero process with complete capture and consistent reason.
